posts.text:
Treat Health | Full-stack Engineer (Elixir, Phoenix LiveView, React) | Helsinki, Finland | ONSITE | Full-time | Compensation in the link below
Treat Health is building healthcare where the right care takes minutes, not days. You describe your concern in your own words, our smart intake asks the follow-up questions a doctor would ask, and a licensed doctor reviews the whole picture and decides on the care. Prescriptions and records go straight to Kanta, Finland's national health archive.
Right now, agentic frontend engineering and agentic mobile app development matter most to us. We expect you to work across the whole stack, with our assistance and tooling.
Stack: Elixir, Phoenix LiveView, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, GCP, Cloudflare and Rust, with Swift and Kotlin for our native mobile apps. Claude is part of everyday work, from planning and coding to review. We care about how well you direct coding agents, not how fast you type.
Small team, high trust: you own problems end to end, with real influence on what we build. Health data stays in the EU, every sign-in uses strong identification, and patient data never ends up in logs.
For now, working on site in Helsinki is a must, and we can't offer relocation or visa support, so you need to already be able to work in Finland. We may hire remotely in the future, so check back later.
Compensation, details and how to apply: https://treat.health/en/careers/full-stack-engineer/

About Lemon.io 
 Lemon.io is a profitable, growing talent marketplace that connects vetted senior engineers with companies that need them. We’ve been in business for 10 years, have 60 people across Ukraine, Europe, Canada, and the US, and process over $16M in annual GMV. We need an engineering leader who can drive that transformation.

 Experience:

posts.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks
posts.text:
C++ docker git go java python security AI/ML rust Typescript  distributed systems SOLID Linux/Unix testing infrastructure
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.
You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.
Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.
How it works
 Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. 
 Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate. 
 Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks. 
 Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them. 
 Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it. 
 Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round. 
 Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another. 
Requirements
 2+ years of professional software engineering 
 Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code) 
 Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++ 
 Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing 
 Regular use of an AI coding tool 
 Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models 
 You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words 
 At least 10 hours a week, starting now 
 A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines) 
Nice to have
 Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure 
 Experience building agent tasks or RL environments 
Terms
 US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you 
 Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms 
 The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us 
 Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork 
Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

posts.title: Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations
posts.text:
Headquarters: Remote - USA
Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.
This is a non-attorney role.  You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.
 As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: 
 Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1. 
 Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions.  Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure.  
 Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions. 
 Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact. 
 Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders. 
 Success in this role looks like: 
 In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals. 
 By 6 months , you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt. 
 By 12 months , you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call

posts.title: Customer Value Architect III
posts.text:
Headquarters: Remote, US
 About Mixpanel 
Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com .
 About the Team 
The Customer Value Architects team sits inside the revenue organization and owns the connection between what customers buy and what they actually get out of Mixpanel. We turn product usage into measurable business outcomes, working across onboarding, adoption, and renewal to make sure customers see the value they signed up for.
 About the Role 
The right candidate is a relationship-first advisor who connects a customer's Mixpanel investment to real outcomes for a defined book of accounts. You'll own the adoption and value plan for each account end to end: understanding why the customer bought Mixpanel, tracking whether they're getting the ROI they expected, and driving the enablement and product usage that gets them there. You'll build trusted relationships with business and technical stakeholders, partner closely with your Account Executive and renewal counterparts, and bring a growing point of view on how customers should think about AI in their product workflows. This role suits someone who can own a project end to end and is ready to start extending their influence beyond their own accounts to the wider team.
 Responsibilities 
 Own the value plan for each account in your portfolio, connecting the business problem that led the customer to buy Mixpanel with the outcomes they measure. 
 Build relationships with business and technical stakeholders, aligning Mixpanel's capabilities to what customers care about most. 
 Run discovery on customer priorities and pain points, and turn what you learn into concrete adoption plans and internal updates. 
 Partner with your Account Executive on expansion and your renewal counterpart on renewal execution, bringing the value case and adoption evidence that supports both. 
 Lead enablement/best practices sessions on dashboard design, funnel analysis, and retention modeling to grow how deeply and widely a customer uses Mixpanel. 
 Monitor usage and health signals and lead business reviews that surface what's working, deepen adoption, and catch risk early. 
 Spot underused features and contracted capabilities, and turn them into clear recommendations for the customer. 
 Triage product questions and issues, solving what you can and routing the rest to the right team. 
 Build a working point of view on a customer's AI maturity, and use Mixpanel's own AI surface to help them build on their product data. 
 Coordinate with GTM, Product, and Engineering on escalations, and share what works with the broader Customer Value Architects team. 
 We're Looking For Someone Who Has 
 4 - 6 years of experience in customer success, consulting, or a related field supporting B2B SaaS accounts, or equivalent experience. 
 A track record of managing relationships across a range of stakeholders, from business partners to technical teams. 
 The ability to translate technical concepts, like data models and product metrics, into terms that land with non-technical stakeholders. 
 Experience turning product usage into a clear story about customer outcomes and ROI. 
 Comfort building and running adoption plans that tie daily work to a customer's larger goals. 
 Hands-on experience with AI or agentic tooling beyond casual use, such as MCP-based workflows or LLM copilots. 
 A collaborative approach to working across account teams and internal partners to move plans forward. 
 Good judgment for prioritizing which accounts and actions need attention first. 
 Bonus Points For 
 Background in product analytics, growth, or data-driven product development. 
 Experience in a technical advisory or professional services capa

posts.title: Head of Technology
posts.text:
Headquarters: New York City
 URL: https://sanctuary.computer 
We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.
 Original job posting link 
 About garden3d 
We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.
Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.
We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.
We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.
 Sanctuary Computer - Development 
At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.
Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.
 XXIX - Design 
When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.
We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.
 Index - Community 
 Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.
We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.
 garden3d TK — Media 
At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.
We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.
Plus, our partner organizations
 Lightphone 
 Mill 
 IngredientAI 
 ⛰️ The Head of Technology Role 
The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.
You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.
This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.
This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.
They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.
They are also how we get better people.

posts.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks (Contract)
posts.text:
Headquarters: Australia 
 URL: https://www.askablelabs.com/ 
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.
You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.
Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.
 How it works 
 Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. 
 Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate. 
 Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks. 
 Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them. 
 Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it. 
 Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round. 
 Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another. 
 Requirements 
 2+ years of professional software engineering 
 Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code) 
 Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++ 
 Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing 
 Regular use of an AI coding tool 
 Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models 
 You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words 
 At least 10 hours a week, starting now 
 A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines) 
 Nice to have 
 Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure 
 Experience building agent tasks or RL environments 
 Terms 
 US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you 
 Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms 
 The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us 
 Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork 
Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer
 To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/askable-software-engineer-ai-coding-tasks-contract

posts.title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure
posts.text:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA or Remote, US
Platform owns the foundation the company runs on: compute and deployment, reliability and on-call, CI/CD and monorepo health, developer environments, the infrastructure that model training and inference run on, and the security boundaries around all of it.
AI and agent tooling is the clearest example. You will contribute to how models are trained and served here, as well as how agents work inside our codebase: the environments they run in, the verification that makes their output trustworthy, and the review paths that keep it all legible. There is no industry standard and you’ll help form our opinions rather than inheriting one.
Our users are other engineers. Expect to spend time with all the other engineering teams, understanding their needs and building a roadmap. The scope is large, so you'll be choosing what to leave alone as much as build.
Architecture decisions here last: this is a small team covering a large surface. You'll have real room to decide things, and you'll stay close to the systems you decide about.
 What you'll own 
 Own our platform: GCP, Kubernetes, Temporal, the GPU fleet behind cloud export, and the deploy and rollback machinery everything ships through. You'll be in the on-call rotation, and we'll expect you to make it quieter and more actionable. 
 The AI enablement substrate: GPU capacity, training and inference pipelines, and the reliability and cost of the systems serving models in production. 
 Cost is an engineering constraint: infrastructure decisions have a number attached and you're expected to make smart trade-offs. As inference grows with usage, the metering and attribution behind those numbers sit with this team. 
 Security comes with the systems you run : identity and access, secrets management, least-privilege boundaries, and supply-chain integrity. 
 Make what you build legible. Infrastructure-as-code that explains itself. Runbooks and in-repo context written for someone jumping in to help. Observability that tells you what failed and why. 
 Improve how the team learns and ships. Form hypotheses, instrument your work, release incrementally, and read results honestly. Strengthen the tooling, standards, tests, observability, and release practices that help the team move quickly without compromising quality. 
 Raise the team’s technical ambition. Provide architectural direction, thoughtful reviews, mentoring, and clear human writing. 
 What you bring 
 Required: 
 You have 8+ years building and operating production distributed systems, or equivalent server-side engineering with a heavy infrastructure focus. 
 You effectively leverage agents to multiply your impact and think critically about how and when to harness AI in your work. 
 You've run systems where failure was expensive, and your opinions about reliability and deployment come from consequences rather than reading. 
 You've carried a pager, commanded an incident, and rolled back before you understood why. 
 You use SLOs and error budgets as operating tools. 
 You’ve used a major cloud provider and Kubernetes in production, with infrastructure-as-code as your default. 
 You've owned an architecture or migration, from planning through launch, whose consequences outlived the project, and you can say what you'd do differently. 
 You've found important unowned work, scoped it, earned buy-in, and delivered it without being handed a spec. 
 You build a minimal repro, read the logs, and write targeted checks to prove a fix works instead of trusting output. 
 Experience that helps: 
 GPU and ML infrastructure: capacity planning, training or inference pipelines, serving cost and latency. If you haven't run a GPU fleet, experience with expensive capacity-constrained systems transfers well. 
 Production security engineering: IAM, secrets, supply chain, least privilege. You don't need to have held a security title, but you should have owned these boundaries for systems you ran.

posts.title: Sunsave | Product Engineer (Mid-Level / Senior) | London, United Kingdom (Holborn) | ONSITE (hybrid, 3 days/week in office) | Full-time
posts.text:
Sunsave | Product Engineer (Mid-Level / Senior) | London, United Kingdom (Holborn) | ONSITE (hybrid, 3 days/week in office) | Full-time
Sunsave is building what replaces your energy supplier. Customers switch to solar and a battery with nothing to pay upfront: kit, install, finance and long-term protection in one package, and the battery trades energy on the grid every day to push their bills towards zero. Founded in 2022, £113m Series A (equity and debt) in 2025, more than 3x growth last year, nearly 90 people.
I lead engineering and data science. Software runs every step of the customer journey: the quote, the finance application, the contract, the install and the battery trading. You'd join a small squad on one area: acquisition (website, quote, finance, contract), installation, in-life (customer app, monitoring, maintenance) or energy (battery optimisation and grid trading).
Product engineers here own problems end to end, from working with the people who use what they build to running it in production. Agents do a lot of the implementation. We expect you to use them every day, delegate the implementation but never the thinking, and own every line you merge. We offer finance and hold customer data, so correctness, auditability and security matter a lot.
Experience: 2+ years running production software for mid-level, 6+ for senior. TypeScript, NestJS, React/Next.js, PostgreSQL and AWS are a plus but not required. Right to work in the UK required.
The interview is built for how we work. No leetcode. A ~45 min async review of a pull request written with AI, then a ~90 min live session where you shape and build a small problem close to our work with your own AI tools.
JD: https://sunsave.notion.site/Sunsave-Product-Engineer-410e7b6... 
Apply: https://ats.welcometothejungle.com/board/sunsave-RTBuAt/job/...

posts.title: DevOps Engineer
posts.text:
DevOps Engineer
Hybrid, 3 days a week in the office
Hong Kong
Full-time
We are looking for a DevOps Engineer to own, scale, and secure our cloud and on-premise computing environments. You will work closely with ML researchers, data scientists, and software engineers to streamline model training, optimize GPU cluster utilization, and automate our continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines.
Core Responsibilities
AI & GPU Infrastructure Management: Provision, monitor, and scale high-performance GPU clusters (NVIDIA H100/A100, CUDA/ROCm setups) for heavy model training and inference workloads.
MLOps & Model Serving Pipelines: Support model deployment, fine-tuning, and low-latency inference optimization using open LLM ecosystems (e.g., vLLM, Triton Inference Server, Llama, Mistral).
CI/CD & Automation: Design, build, and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines for both software services and ML model artifacts using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or ArgoCD.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Manage cloud resources (AWS, GCP, or Azure) repeatably using tools like Terraform or Pulumi.
Containerization & Orchestration: Deploy, scale, and manage distributed containerized workloads using Kubernetes (K8s), Docker, and KubeFlow or Ray.
Observability & Reliability: Implement logging, tracing, and metric dashboards (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) to track cluster health, GPU memory/utilization, and inference latency.
Security & Governance: Enforce DevSecOps practices, secret management (HashiCorp Vault), container image scanning, and access controls tailored for sensitive AI datasets and models.
Required Qualifications
Experience: 3+ years of experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), or Cloud/Platform Engineering, with exposure to MLOps or AI/ML workloads.
Cloud & Containers: Strong hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure, alongside production Kubernetes and Docker management.
Scripting & Programming: Proficiency in Python, Bash/Shell, or Go for automation and tooling.
IaC & CI/CD: Demonstrated mastery of Terraform, GitOps workflows, and automated testing/deployment pipelines.
AI Ecosystem Knowledge: Familiarity with GPU node provisioning, distributed storage for massive datasets, and model serving runtimes.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with LLM orchestration frameworks (LangChain, Ray Serve, vLLM).
Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
Active cloud or Kubernetes certifications (e.g., CKA, AWS/GCP DevOps Engineer).
Apply: https://round1.work/listings/listing_tenant_a741427d-313d-41...

posts.text:
Prior Labs | Berlin, Freiburg, NYC | ONSITE | Full-time | https://priorlabs.ai 
We build foundation models for tables. TabPFN takes your whole dataset as context and predicts in one forward pass - no training, no tuning - after pre-training only on synthetic data from causal priors. TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover; the open models have 4M+ downloads and run in production from liquid biopsy to rail maintenance. Since July we're an independent lab inside SAP with €1B+ over four years; models stay open-weight and research stays public.
We're hiring engineers:
Infrastructure Engineer - multi-cluster GPU training on Slurm, GCP today and more providers in 2027. The compute budget is tens of millions a year, and you own it.
ML Engineer, Backend - own inference end to end: latency, batching and memory on million-row inputs, across our API, customer VPCs and open weights.
Full Stack Developer - the product where data scientists, agents and our models meet. TypeScript/React + Python/FastAPI.
Also hiring: Research Scientists and Research Engineers (Foundation Model), Applied Scientist (NYC), PhD research interns, GTM and ops roles. We sponsor visas and help with relocation.
~45 people, led by Frank Hutter, advised by Yann LeCun and Bernhard Schölkopf.

Sortrace | Computer Vision Engineer, Junior Frontend Engineer | REMOTE (Europe), hybrid Norrköping or Stockholm | Full-time | https://sortrace.com 
Sortrace is a small cleantech AI company in Sweden. Cameras on waste collection trucks and trained vision models flag material in the wrong fraction when bins are emptied. Customers use our platform to review deviations, images, and insights.
We're hiring for two roles on a small team with short decision paths.
Computer Vision Engineer
- Train, evaluate, and improve deep learning models for real-world image analysis on our existing platform (datasets, augmentation, architecture experiments, precision/robustness/performance).

Junior Frontend Engineer

Compensation: monthly salary by agreement; equity/options possible.
Apply: jobs@sortrace.com or https://sortrace.com/careers , subject line with the role name. CV role: short note on CV experience + links to projects/GitHub. Frontend role: what you built, how, and a link or demo if you have one. Questions welcome; we reply to applicants.

posts.title: Nirvana Robotics | Mechanical Engineer, Electrical Engineer, Robotic Controls Engineer | New York, NY | ONSITE | Full-time | $220K-$300K
posts.text:
Nirvana Robotics | Mechanical Engineer, Electrical Engineer, Robotic Controls Engineer | New York, NY | ONSITE | Full-time | $220K-$300K
Nirvana Robotics builds humanoid robots with robotic arms that work in industrial environments. Their hardware team in NYC is growing, and each of these roles owns a subsystem end to end on physical robots. I'm a recruiter at Niuro, Nirvana's hiring partner for these roles; the links below go to our application form and I read every application myself.
Mechanical Engineer ($230K-$260K): mechanical design of robotic arms and manipulators: joints, actuators, transmissions, end effectors. You optimize for torque density, backdrivability and stiffness, prototype with additive and precision machining, and take assemblies to production. GD&T, tolerance stack-ups, SolidWorks (or Creo/NX/Onshape).
Apply: https://app.niuro.io/source/H4yYHesP?ref=ps_EBRp88zU7jcdRZm8... 
Electrical Engineer ($220K-$250K): electrical architecture for arms and humanoids: power distribution, motor-driver boards, sensor PCBs, harnessing. Multilayer mixed-signal and high-current layout in Altium, BLDC drivers and current sensing, bench bring-up and DFM with PCBA partners. EtherCAT, CAN or BMS is a plus.
Apply: https://app.niuro.io/source/BeVx3CrN?ref=ps_5biniQ0FTotNxfmT... 
Robotic Controls Engineer ($270K-$300K): low-level control for multi-DOF arms: joint-level actuation, impedance/admittance and whole-body control, sim-to-real. PID/LQR/state-space, MoveIt or cuRobo, C++ and Python, ROS 2.
Apply: https://app.niuro.io/source/gUNqx8Lj?ref=ps_BdIAhZPrP7yQt2P4... 
For all three: hands-on work on real robot hardware (arms, grippers, mobile manipulators, actuated joints or humanoids). Mechanical and Electrical: 5+ years with a bachelor's or 3+ with a master's. Controls: roughly BS + 4 years, MS + 2 or a PhD. US-based; relocation to NYC within the US is supported. Visa sponsorship is not available.

posts.title: Lumen Labs | Robotics/Hardware Engineer, Simulation Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE | Full-time | $150k–200k + equity | https://lumenr
posts.text:
Lumen Labs | Robotics/Hardware Engineer, Simulation Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE | Full-time | $150k–200k + equity | https://lumenresearch.co 
Howdy! Lumen Labs is building the cognitive layer for physical AI. Nearly every major robotics effort today teaches machines by showing them thousands of hours of human teleoperation. We think that paradigm has a ceiling, and we’re working on nature-inspired architectures for unstructured environments (construction sites, mining, pipelines, battlefield). Pre-seed, backed by top VC funds and operators from robotics/AI companies. Today we run wheeled navigation, we’re dipping our toes into drones, and we’re eyeing weirder platforms like home inspection.
We’re a small team hiring two engineers who will work closely with each other and with our model engineer:
ROBOTICS / HARDWARE ENGINEER: Own the hardware and infrastructure that keeps our research platforms running: the ROS2 (Humble) stack across onboard and offboard compute, sensor integration and calibration (LiDAR, depth, IMU, encoders), the safety pipeline during autonomous runs, and getting trained policies onto real hardware. Will be hands-on with real mobile robots (UART, encoders, PWM, IMU, LiDAR), strong Python + embedded, comfortable reading code you didn’t write, and can debug hardware and firmware at the same time. Full posting: https://desert-bearskin-26d.notion.site/Robotics-Engineer-Ro... 
SIMULATION ENGINEER: Own “the gauntlet,” our test library for putting new architectures through their paces: a Gymnasium-style interface on both sides (environment and model) so anything built to spec is compatible with everything else. Mostly MuJoCo and Gazebo today, moving toward Isaac Sim, and some other more bespoke sims. You will be building task simulators for training and testing and keeping them running (GPS-denied drone nav, construction sites, boat cleaning, forklifts, abstract control), including physics, honest sensor models, digital twins of our real platforms, domain randomization, and the sim compute. Dungeon Master. If you have built or substantially rebuilt a simulator of some kind (robotics/RL is closest, but a physics-based game, scientific sim, or flight sim mod counts) this would be a good role for you. Comfortable with the Gymnasium/dm_control way of thinking, can pick up GPU-vectorized sim (MJX, Isaac Lab, JAX) quickly, and test-driven. Full posting: https://desert-bearskin-26d.notion.site/Simulation-Engineer-... 
Email hi@lumenresearch.co, mention HN and which role, and tell us about a project you’ve built. If you can link to a trained policy running on real hardware (robotics) or a simulator you built or fixed and something you trained inside it (sim), you go to the top of the pile.

posts.text:
Estuary | US-Based / Remote | Full-time – https://estuary.dev/ 
Estuary is a VC-backed, post–Series A startup powering real-time data replication and transform — from sub-second CDC replication to terabyte-scale OLAP data flows. We’re open-source, developer-first, and focused on making data movement radically simpler across both our Platform and Applications layers.
We’re hiring for:
Head of Engineering — Own the engineering function end-to-end as a partner to our founder CTO: strategy, people, delivery, and operations across a compact but high-leverage team. You’ll grow the leaders already running our teams, set technical strategy jointly with the CTO, and be accountable for what engineering ships and what it costs.
Senior Systems Engineer (Control & Data Plane) — Build the high-performance backbone of our platform: the orchestration, distributed state, and stream transport that keep pipelines at sub-second latency under massive throughput. You’ll work primarily in Rust on fault tolerance, consensus, and networking, and help set the bar for correctness and performance across the team.
Product Manager — Own product areas end-to-end, working closely with engineering and design to shape the roadmap and deliver a great developer experience. Engage with users, translate real-world use cases into product decisions, and help define how modern data infrastructure should feel to build with.
Head of Product Marketing — Lead product marketing as we bring real-time, agent-ready data pipelines to technical buyers, partnering closely with our Head of Marketing, Developer Relations, and the founders. Own positioning, messaging, launches, and competitive narrative, turning what our engineers ship into stories data teams actually care about.
Solutions Engineer — Partner with sales and customers from the first technical call through production, running discovery, demos, and proofs of concept for data engineering and platform teams. You’ll design CDC, streaming, and batch pipelines on Estuary, solve real integration problems hands-on, and feed what you learn back to Product and Engineering.
Customer Success Manager — Own the post-sale relationship for our data engineering and platform customers as our first CS hire. You’ll build onboarding, account health monitoring, and the expansion playbook from scratch while staying technical enough to resolve most issues yourself.
Senior Compliance Engineer — Own our GDPR and PCI DSS programs while keeping our audited SOC 2 and HIPAA programs running smoothly, alongside hands-on ownership of identity, endpoint, and SaaS estate management. This is a governance-first role for someone who has run a compliance program end-to-end, not just contributed to one.
What we’re looking for: People who care about building reliable, maintainable systems and processes and enjoy working with complex APIs, data flows, or customer relationships. We value curiosity, clear communication, and a willingness to learn.
Bonus points for experience with CDC tools, open source contributions, or fast-paced startups.
To apply: Email your resume to careers@estuary.dev

posts.title: Blockrotate| Senior Systems / Rust Engineer | Remote (US/EU timezones preferred) | Full-time | $130k - $170k + Equity
posts.text:
Blockrotate| Senior Systems / Rust Engineer | Remote (US/EU timezones preferred) | Full-time | $130k - $170k + Equity
Blockrotate ( https://blockrotate.com ) builds low-latency copy-trading and execution infrastructure for Polymarket and prediction markets.
Copy trading on prediction markets has strange market microstructure. Unlike deep perp DEXes (Binance, Hyperliquid), Polymarket orderbooks are bounded, often thin, and subject to severe adverse selection. When a high-volume leader buys, the book moves immediately. If followers lag by a few hundred milliseconds, or if a platform taxes every order with a 50bps fee, follower alpha drops to zero.
Most existing tools in this space either hit users with high per-trade taker fees or ask them to export and paste their master private key into a database. We took a different approach: isolated per-bot deposit wallets (non-custodial via EIP-1967/1271 proxies) and co-located autonomous Rust workers running delta-sync loops directly against the Polymarket CLOB.
Stack:
- Backend: Rust, Tokio, Axum, Protobuf over WebSockets, SQLite (WAL mode)
- Trading Engine: Custom Polymarket CLOB & Data API clients, EIP-712 signing, dynamic slippage ladders, momentum filters, circuit breakers
- Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
What you’d actually work on:
- Squeezing latency out of the execution hot path (delta position calculation, order placement, nonce handling, fill verification).
- Building better execution protection: momentum filters to dodge toxic order flow, fill stabilization windows, and handling thin book liquidity without moving the market against yourself.
- Scaling worker orchestration: our C2 server talks Protobuf to distributed bot workers with monotonic sequence IDs and autonomous reconnect failover. As bot volume scales, we need to keep state reconciliation bulletproof.
- Investigating and exploiting prediction market quirks (rebate structures, orderbook snapshotting, MEV/relayer bottlenecks).
What we look for:
- Strong async Rust experience (Tokio, concurrency, practical memory management).
- Experience dealing with websockets, exchange orderbooks, or trading infrastructure
shoot an email to jobs@blockrotate.com and tell us why you would be a good fit for us.

Quantum Rise is an AI-forward consulting startup serving the mid-market in the US and larger enterprises in LATAM. We see companies in multiple industries struggling to understand how to leverage artificial intelligence in their day-to-day operations, trying to understand what their existing workforce now needs to know, or trying to understand whether they're about to be disrupted and need to change how their existing processes work. Many have business problems which "traditional" machine learning could help with even prior to the current GenAI hype cycle, but for whatever reason hadn't prioritized doing until now. Many have employees looking to incorporate agentic AI safely and effectively across different business areas. We try and help getting a handle around these issues and designing outcome-driven solutions.
Agentic AI Engineer: You'll work directly with clients to benchmark, train and deploy agentic systems for industry-specific problems. We're looking for someone deeply embedded in agentic engineering practice across vendors and platforms. Companies are looking for ways to leverage agentic systems to upskill their practitioners and need help navigating a new, powerful scary world.
AI Solutions Engineer: You're someone who has experience in traditional machine learning and data science applications in addition to more recent agentic systems.
We think of these two roles as complementary -- agentic AI solutioners help clients understand the forefront, whereas pure AI solutioners help them pick and build the right solution even if it isn't an LLM.
Both are front-facing development roles for someone who loves both tech and tackling real business problems. We love people with prior experience in multiple industries.
To apply, send me an email at julian.berman at quantumrise.com, mentioning HN and including your CV.

In fact, on the back of some recent successes, we are gearing up to build up a team and dramatically expand this work. posts.title: Subimage (YC W25) | Founding Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE (5 days/week) | Full-time | $170K–$230K + 0.5%–1.0% equity | https://subi
posts.text:
Subimage (YC W25) | Founding Engineer | San Francisco, CA | ONSITE (5 days/week) | Full-time | $170K–$230K + 0.5%–1.0% equity | https://subimage.io 
Hihi, I'm Alex, co-founder and CEO. Subimage maps infrastructure the way an attacker does so security teams at scale-ups and enterprises can find and fix problems. We're built on Cartography ( https://cartography.dev ), the open source infra mapping tool we helped create at Lyft and donated to the CNCF. It runs at over 70 companies, including 7 in the Fortune 100.
We're a tiny seed-stage team and our customers are companies your parents have heard of. We have more demand than we can build for, which is why this post exists. This is a chance to get in on the ground floor of something big (or to find out quickly that it won't work; just being upfront about it).
Some of the problems you'd be working on:
- Vulnerability triage with real context: is the asset internet-facing, through which services, is the vulnerable function actually reachable in code, are there compensating controls, and what sensitive data does it reach once exploited, across how many hops.
- Proving that the security fixes our agent proposes won't break anything.
- A near-real-time, self-updating map of an environment so you can see an attack as it happens, plus "time travel" in the graph so you can replay it afterward.
- Teaching an agent to answer questions about a large graph quickly, with only the context it needs and without making mistakes.
- Determining who owns a given resource from messy signals like tags, actions, logs, and files.

posts.title: ArtCraft | Senior Engineers | SF (Onsite) / Atlanta (Onsite) | $150-$250k + Equity | https://getartcraft.com
posts.text:
ArtCraft | Senior Engineers | SF (Onsite) / Atlanta (Onsite) | $150-$250k + Equity | https://getartcraft.com 
Those fucking rent-seeking hyperscalers took the internet away from you, and we’re going to give it back to you and to everyone.
Web 1.0 was great - we had IRC, file sharing, third party chat clients. There were personal websites, forums. Flash was a format kids could use. Everything supported embedding and uploading. Websites actually had APIs and RSS. File sharing, FTP, MP3s, discs, owned media.
Broadband brought our parents and grandparents online, but the shift to the non-technical majority created an opportunity to grossly oversimplify everything. Everything dumbed down into a pre-packaged product. Startups began turning their offerings into walled gardens. Platforms took precedence over protocols. APIs and access and data export went away. And then the rent-seeking began. The era of ownership ended.
Corporate Memphis. Jesus Christ.
We’ve rallied a massive community to build MIT/Apache-licensed alternatives to Adobe, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Autodesk, SolidWorks, Slack, Discord, Unreal Engine, OpenRouter, RunPod, and more. The goal is full feature parity, with code anyone can own, inspect, modify, and build on.
We’re digesting second-class apps and platforms into first-class applications, libraries, and APIs with full MCP support. We’re distilling out the good parts, and we’re building the connective tissue that draws them together.
100% of the internet is going to be open source soon, and we’re going to force it open. Loudly.
We have eight figures in run rate revenue, over 20M app downloads and growing. Our community is the best part, and it’s energetic like a wildfire. Everyone resonates with our mission.
We’re missionaries, not mercenaries. We are going to slay the incumbents by being better. Our motto is Google’s old motto - “Don't be evil (tm)”.
We’re a tiny team looking for strong engineers to own major parts of the product: desktop apps, lots of completely open source backend infrastructure, agent workflows, agentic app factories. Stack: Rust, a sprinkle of TypeScript/React, egui, Tauri, MySQL/Postgres, Redis, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes. Lots and lots of Rust. We’re systems engineers by trade, but we like to vibe code Rust. Did I say Rust? Rust. Rust Rust Rust. Maybe that's a filter.
You have to be self-directed and independent. If you want to open source Salesforce with half your time, do it! If you want to work on Solidworks 3D printing applications, great! Writing music apps and DAWs? Go for it! Custom Discord/Slack clients for our custom, completely open source chat API and platform? Hell yeah. Our organization is flat, and we're going to go after everybody and everything.
Everything you build here will be open source. We have no private repos.
We can reclaim the internet. That’s our mission.
Want to know more about us? Look up “Adobe ArtCraft” on YouTube / TikTok / your platform of choice.
If this resonates with you, email hn@storyteller.ai with your Github, a little about yourself and something you’ve built. Write the sentence, “don’t take my RAM, Sam!” so we know you’re one of the good guys.

posts.text:
Stratirus (a Tennetech company) | AI Developer + Linux Admin (junior to mid) | REMOTE (US only, Central Time hours) | US work authorization required, no sponsorship | Full-time or part-time, contract or hire | $65k to $100k | No agencies
Our optional take-home is a broken Ubuntu server: a service that won't stay up, a nightly report that hasn't gone out in days, and a disk that keeps filling. Fix it, write a script that heals a fresh box, and build a small read-only MCP tool so an AI agent can check on it. 60 to 90 minutes, unpaid, no LeetCode. If that sounds like fun, read on.
We're a small and growing AI and Microsoft 365 consultancy in Franklin, TN. We build AI agents and automation for small and mid-sized businesses, and harden and run the systems underneath: Microsoft 365 tenants, SharePoint, and Linux boxes. We're AI-agnostic and use what fits the client, mostly Claude Code, the Microsoft 365 stack with Copilot and Copilot Studio, Gemini and Gemini Studio, and Oracle OBI. PeopleSoft experience is a plus. You'll work directly with clients, so explaining things clearly to a small-business owner matters as much as the code. Early-career and career-switchers welcome.
We expect you to use AI every day. What we hire for is knowing when it's wrong, so one of our three application questions asks about a time it fooled you.
To apply, email your resume to hiring@stratirus.com with short answers to: a time a client or boss made an unreasonable demand and how you handled it; a time an AI confidently gave you a wrong answer you followed, and how you caught it; and something you've built with AI that you still use. Work samples get strong preference. We read every application ourselves and reply to everyone, so please write your answers yourself.
Process: email application, a 45-minute video call where you walk us through something you've built, then a conversation about the role.
Remote within the US only, Central Time business hours. Must be legally authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship, now or in the future. No recruiters or agencies, please.

posts.text:
MixRank (YC S11) | Software Engineers | 100% Remote (Global) | Full-Time MixRank processes petabytes of data every month through web crawling. Hundreds of customers use our data products, including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries such as finance, recruiting, sales, marketing, and security. We’re a fully remote company with a global footprint across 20+ countries. We’re growing, profitable, employee-owned, and have no dependence on outside funding. Applicants from all geographies and backgrounds are welcome. We’re looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job, but something they genuinely love to do. We’re obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team. Our codebase is friendly to new contributors. You’ll have a fully functional development environment within hours through full automation and will be pushing commits on your first day. Deployments to production happen multiple times per day and finish in under two minutes.Effectively all of our codebase is written in Python, Rust, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Nix. The core technologies you’ll need familiarity with to be productive are Python, PostgreSQL, Linux, and Git.
We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We run two datacenters with high-performance servers we’ve built ourselves, capable of handling the volumes of data we process. We’ve implemented our own distributed file system, perform full-scale web crawls, and download and run static analysis on the entire universe of published Android APKs and iOS IPAs.
Unlike a typical startup where you might spend half your time in meetings and the other half fixing Jira tickets, at MixRank you’ll challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that help you grow as an individual. We’re continuously hiring for the positions below; these aren’t singular roles that close once filled. Our philosophy is that the candidate is more important than the position. For each new member of the team, we design a custom role and responsibilities around their interests. Other companies may create a long list of specific requirements with the expectation that you’ll exactly replace someone on the team or fit a role defined by committee. MixRank is more pragmatic: we first get excited about bringing a unique individual onto the team, then figure out the best way to support their specific talents.

We’re looking for remote junior engineers with 0–3 years of professional software experience and 5+ years of curiosity exploring computers, programming, and technical hobby projects.
This is an open-ended entry role with mentorship and diverse opportunities to work across all areas of our product: databases, distributed systems, infrastructure and tooling, data analysis, machine learning, frontend/backend web development, APIs, data mining, data modeling, and more.
To stand out, please highlight what makes you unique: passion for computing, curiosity and side projects, work ethic, niche research, or anything else that shows how you think and build.
Ideally, you’ve already graduated. But if you still have one or more years left of school, please feel free to apply anyway. If you’re the right fit for the team, we’ll figure out a way to accommodate your schedule.

Software Engineer - Remote (Global), Full-Time

posts.company: University of Cambridge, University of Manchester
posts.text:
University of Cambridge, University of Manchester | PhD in AI / Earth Observation / Environmental Science | ONSITE | UK home fee status only | £30k tax-free annual stipend
Our group at Cambridge works on Earth Observation foundation models (Tessera: v1 https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20380 , v2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03949 , https://geotessera.org/ ) and we've started a collaboration with Manchester to understand how they can be used to improve pollution models and then environmental decision making in general. This involves training new models and doing high-resolution inference across national or even global scales, as well as figuring out how to use that data to help policymakers make better decisions.
As part of this work we have a PhD studentship through the joint Manchester-Cambridge Centre for Doctoral Training for AI in Decision Making for Complex Systems. This involves one year at Manchester doing taught postgraduate study and then three years at Cambridge for the PhD.
Our work is all open source and involves solving significant compute and data challenges. Training our current-generation model takes ~250k GPU hours and a single year of global inference needs to move over 5.5 petabytes of data through the inference pipeline. This project would suit someone with strong machine learning and software engineering experience. We can help you build the atmospheric science and Earth Observation skills.
We are a highly collaborative group who spend our time not only on foundational research but also on developing applications with practitioners and decision makers. Our work sees use in many industrial, academic and government environments for problems like crop classification, tree species mapping and change detection.
You can find out more here: https://www.findaphd.com/phds/project/from-satellite-to-stre... - if you have questions about the project you can contact me, Sadiq Jaffer, at sj514@cam.ac.uk . For questions about the application process you'll want aidecisionscdt@manchester.ac.uk .
Application deadline is Friday 4th of December with a course start date of September 2027.
